chapters.title: Return to Me
chapters.html:
Zechariah 1

Return to Me

1In the eighth month, in the second year of Darius, the word of the LORD came to Zechariah son of Berechiah, son of Iddo, the prophet, saying,

2"The LORD was very angry with your fathers.

3So say to them: This is what the LORD of hosts says: Return to Me, declares the LORD of hosts, and I will return to you, says the LORD of hosts.

4Do not be like your fathers, to whom the former prophets called out, saying, 'This is what the LORD of hosts says: Turn, please, from your evil ways and your evil deeds'; but they did not listen or pay attention to Me, declares the LORD.

5Your fathers — where are they? The prophets — do they live forever?

6But My words and My statutes, which I commanded My servants the prophets, did they not overtake your fathers? Then they turned and said, 'As the LORD of hosts purposed to do to us, according to our ways and our deeds, so He has done with us.'"

The Man Among the Myrtles

7On the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month, which is the month of Shebat, in the second year of Darius, the word of the LORD came to Zechariah son of Berechiah, son of Iddo, the prophet, saying:

8I saw in the night a man riding on a red horse, and he was standing among the myrtle trees in the hollow; and behind him were red, sorrel and white horses.

9I said, "What are these, my lord?" The messenger who talked with me said to me, "I will show you what these are."

10The man standing among the myrtle trees answered and said, "These are the ones the LORD has sent to walk about over the earth."

11They answered the messenger of the LORD who was standing among the myrtle trees and said, "We have walked about over the earth, and the whole earth sits still and at rest."

12Then the messenger of the LORD answered and said, "LORD of hosts, how long will You have no compassion on Jerusalem and on the cities of Judah, with which You have been indignant these seventy years?"

13The LORD answered the messenger who talked with me with good words, comforting words.

14The messenger who talked with me said to me, "Call out: This is what the LORD of hosts says: I am exceedingly jealous for Jerusalem and for Zion,

15and I am very angry with the nations that are at ease; for I was angry only a little, and they helped the evil along.

16Therefore this is what the LORD says: I have returned to Jerusalem with compassion; My house will be built in it, declares the LORD of hosts, and a measuring line will be stretched out over Jerusalem.

17Call out again: This is what the LORD of hosts says: My cities will again overflow with good; the LORD will again comfort Zion and will again choose Jerusalem."

Four Horns and Four Craftsmen

18I lifted up my eyes and saw four horns.

19I said to the messenger who talked with me, "What are these?" He said to me, "These are the horns that scattered Judah, Israel and Jerusalem."

20Then the LORD showed me four craftsmen.

21I said, "What are these coming to do?" He said, "These are the horns that scattered Judah, so that no one could lift up his head; and these have come to terrify them, to throw down the horns of the nations who lifted up a horn against the land of Judah to scatter it."

Notes

  • v1 "In the eighth month, in the second year of Darius… Zechariah son of Berechiah, son of Iddo" — two months after Haggai's first word (Haggai 1:1). Ezra names the two prophets together, Haggai the prophet and Zechariah son of Iddo (Ezra 5:1), and a Zechariah heads the house of Iddo among the priests (Nehemiah 12:16). Jesus names Zechariah son of Berechiah, whom you murdered between the sanctuary and the altar (Matthew 23:35); the Zechariah killed in the court of the house of the LORD in Chronicles is son of Jehoiada (2 Chronicles 24:20–21). Zekharyah, Zechariah, has the letters of zakhar, remember, with the LORD's name.

  • vv2–3 "The LORD was very angry with your fathers… Return to Me… and I will return to you" — qatsaf… qetsef, word for word was angry with anger. Shuvu elai… ve-ashuv aleikhem, return to Me… and I will return to you, one verb both ways: the people's turning and the LORD's. The book's call is answered in v16, I have returned to Jerusalem. Declares and says the LORD of hosts three times in one verse.

  • vv4–6 "the former prophets… Turn, please, from your evil ways… did they not overtake your fathers?" — the former prophets called in these words, Turn now, each of you, from his evil way and from the evil of your deeds (Jeremiah 25:5). The prophets died and the fathers died, but the words did not: hissigu, overtake, is the verb of the law's curses, all these curses will come on you and overtake you (Deuteronomy 28:15). Zamam, purposed, is the verb of The LORD has done what He purposed (Lamentations 2:17).

  • vv7–8 "the month of Shebat… a man riding on a red horse… among the myrtle trees in the hollow" — Shebat is named only here. Hadassim, myrtle trees, as in instead of the brier the myrtle will come up (Isaiah 55:13); the Greek has the shaded mountains, harim, a word of similar sound. Ba-metsulah, in the hollow, is the word of the depths of the sea (Jonah 2:3; Micah 7:19). Seruqqim, sorrel, a reddish brown; the Greek adds dappled.

  • vv9–11 "my lord… The messenger who talked with me… We have walked about over the earth" — adoni, my lord, is the address to a superior, here the messenger. Ha-mal'akh ha-dover bi, the messenger who talked with me, guides the visions that follow. The riders patrol as Satan did, From roaming over the earth and from walking about on it (Job 1:7). Yoshevet ve-shoqatet, sits still and at rest, as in The whole earth is at rest and quiet (Isaiah 14:7): the nations are at peace.

  • vv12–13 "how long will You have no compassion… these seventy years?… good words, comforting words" — ad matai, how long, Habakkuk's cry (Habakkuk 2:6), now from the messenger of the LORD himself, who pleads with the LORD of hosts. Seventy years is Jeremiah's number, When seventy years are completed for Babylon, I will attend to you (Jeremiah 29:10). Devarim nichumim, comforting words, from the verb of Comfort, comfort My people (Isaiah 40:1).

  • vv14–16 "I am exceedingly jealous for Jerusalem… the nations that are at ease… a measuring line will be stretched out" — qinneti… qin'ah gedolah, word for word I am jealous with a great jealousy, as in the LORD was jealous for His land (Joel 2:18). Ha-sha'ananim, at ease, is Amos's word, Woe to those at ease in Zion (Amos 6:1), now said of the nations. Azru le-ra'ah, helped the evil along: the LORD was angry a little, and the nations went further. The measuring line was once stretched out to destroy, He stretched out the measuring line (Lamentations 2:8); now it is stretched out to build, as in The measuring line will go out farther (Jeremiah 31:39).

  • vv18–21 "four horns… four craftsmen… to throw down the horns of the nations" — a horn is strength, as in All the horns of the wicked I will cut off (Psalm 75:10), and He has raised the horn of your foes (Lamentations 2:17); what the four stand for, the vision does not say. Charashim, craftsmen, are smiths and workers in wood and stone, as in I have created the smith who blows the fire of coals (Isaiah 54:16). Le-hacharid, to terrify, is the verb of no one shall make them afraid (Micah 4:4). In the Hebrew text vv18–21 are 2:1–4; the English numbering is followed, and the Greek follows it too.

chapters.title: A Wall of Fire All Around
chapters.html:
Zechariah 2

The Man with a Measuring Line

1I lifted up my eyes and saw a man with a measuring line in his hand.

2I said, "Where are you going?" He said to me, "To measure Jerusalem, to see how great its width is and how great its length."

3Then the messenger who talked with me went out, and another messenger went out to meet him,

4and said to him, "Run, speak to that young man: Jerusalem will be lived in as open villages, because of the great number of people and animals inside it.

5I Myself will be to her, declares the LORD, a wall of fire all around, and I will be the glory inside her."

Flee from the Land of the North

6Up! Up! Flee from the land of the north, declares the LORD; for I have spread you abroad like the four winds of the heavens, declares the LORD.

7Up! Escape to Zion, you who live with the daughter of Babylon!

8For this is what the LORD of hosts says: After glory He has sent me to the nations that plundered you; for whoever touches you touches the pupil of His eye.

9For I am about to shake My hand over them, and they will become plunder for those who served them. Then you will know that the LORD of hosts has sent me.

10Sing aloud and rejoice, daughter of Zion, for I am about to come, and I will dwell among you, declares the LORD.

11Many nations will join themselves to the LORD on that day and will be My people, and I will dwell among you; and you will know that the LORD of hosts has sent me to you.

12The LORD will take Judah as His portion on the holy ground, and will again choose Jerusalem.

13Silence, all flesh, before the LORD! For He has roused Himself from His holy dwelling.

Notes

  • vv1–2 "a man with a measuring line in his hand… To measure Jerusalem" — in the Hebrew text vv1–13 are 2:5–17; the English numbering is followed, and the Greek follows it too. The third vision, after the horsemen (1:8) and the horns (1:18). The measuring line promised in 1:16 is now in a man's hand, as Ezekiel saw a man with a linen cord and a measuring reed in his hand (Ezekiel 40:3).

  • vv3–5 "Jerusalem will be lived in as open villages… a wall of fire all around, and I will be the glory inside her" — perazot, open villages, without walls, the word of a land of unwalled villages… all of them living without walls (Ezekiel 38:11): the city will be too full to be walled. Ehyeh, I will be, the word God gave as His name, I AM THE ONE WHO WILL BE (Exodus 3:14). The wall of fire recalls the pillar of fire that went before Israel (Exodus 13:21), and the glory inside her is the glory Ezekiel saw coming back, The glory of the God of Israel was coming from the east (Ezekiel 43:2).

  • vv6–7 "Up! Up! Flee from the land of the north… Escape to Zion, you who live with the daughter of Babylon!" — hoy hoy, a cry to rouse, Up! Up!, the word that elsewhere is Woe. The call is Isaiah's and Jeremiah's, Go out from Babylon, flee from the Chaldeans! (Isaiah 48:20), Flee from the middle of Babylon (Jeremiah 51:6), to those still in exile. Himmaleti, escape, the verb of Joel 2:32. For I have spread you abroad like the four winds, the Greek has from the four winds of the heaven I will gather you.

  • vv8–9 "After glory He has sent me… whoever touches you touches the pupil of His eye… I am about to shake My hand over them" — achar kavod shelachani, after glory He has sent me, is obscure: after the glory of v5, or for the sake of glory; who me is, the prophet or the messenger, the verse does not make plain. Bavat eino, the pupil of His eye, a word found only here, as the law says of Jacob, He guarded him as the pupil of His eye (Deuteronomy 32:10). Menif, shake, as in the hand that the LORD of hosts shakes over it (Isaiah 19:16). The plunderers become plunder for those who served them.

  • vv10–11 "Sing aloud and rejoice, daughter of Zion… I will dwell among you… Many nations will join themselves to the LORD" — ronni ve-simchi bat Tsiyyon, the cry of Zephaniah 3:14. Ve-shakhanti ve-tokhekh, I will dwell among you, the promise of the tabernacle, Let them make Me a sanctuary, and I will dwell among them (Exodus 25:8), now for Zion and for the nations. Ve-nilvu, will join themselves, as in The foreigners who join themselves to the LORD (Isaiah 56:6); it is the verb of Levi's name, this time, my husband will be joined to me… Therefore he called his name Levi (Genesis 29:34). Will be My people is the covenant word, I will take you to Myself as a people (Exodus 6:7), given to many nations.

  • vv12–13 "His portion on the holy ground… Silence, all flesh, before the LORD!" — chelqo, His portion, as in the LORD's portion is His people (Deuteronomy 32:9). Admat ha-qodesh, the holy ground, is found only here; it is the ground of the bush, the place you are standing on is holy ground (Exodus 3:5), now the whole land. Has, silence, as in Habakkuk 2:20 and Zephaniah 1:7. Ne'or, He has roused Himself, from ur, the verb of Joel 3:9, mi-me'on qodsho, from His holy dwelling, as in Look down from Your holy dwelling, from heaven (Deuteronomy 26:15).

chapters.title: A Brand Snatched from the Fire
chapters.html:
Zechariah 3

Joshua the High Priest

1Then He showed me Joshua the high priest standing before the messenger of the LORD, and Satan standing at his right hand to accuse him.

2The LORD said to Satan, "The LORD rebuke you, Satan! The LORD who has chosen Jerusalem rebuke you! Is not this man a brand snatched from the fire?"

3Joshua was clothed in filthy garments, standing before the messenger.

4The messenger answered and said to those standing before him, "Take the filthy garments off him." To Joshua he said, "See, I have put away your iniquity from you, and I will clothe you in festal robes."

5Then I said, "Let them put a clean turban on his head." They put the clean turban on his head and clothed him in garments, while the messenger of the LORD stood by.

6The messenger of the LORD solemnly charged Joshua, saying,

7"This is what the LORD of hosts says: If you walk in My ways and keep My watch, then you will govern My house and guard My courts, and I will give you a place to walk among these who stand here.

My Servant the Branch

8Hear, please, Joshua the high priest, you and your companions who sit before you, for they are men who are a portent: I am about to bring My servant the Branch.

9Here is the stone that I have set before Joshua: on one stone are seven eyes. I am about to engrave its inscription, declares the LORD of hosts, and I will remove the iniquity of that land in one day.

10On that day, declares the LORD of hosts, each of you will invite his neighbor under his vine and under his fig tree."

Notes

  • vv1–2 "Then He showed me… Satan standing at his right hand to accuse him… The LORD rebuke you, Satan!" — va-yar'eni, He showed me, with no name; in 1:20 it is the LORD showed me, and the Greek has the Lord showed me here. Ha-satan, Satan, with the article, as in Job (Job 1:6), is word for word the accuser, and le-sitno, to accuse him, is the same root: the accuser stands to accuse. The word is a plain noun in the messenger of the LORD took his stand in the road as an adversary against him (Numbers 22:22), and the right hand is the accuser's place in let an accuser stand at his right hand (Psalm 109:6). Ud mutsal me-esh, a brand snatched from the fire, are Amos's words, you were like a brand snatched from the burning (Amos 4:11): Joshua and his people are what is left after the fire of exile.

  • vv3–5 "filthy garments… I have put away your iniquity… a clean turban" — tso'im, filthy, is the word for excrement, as in the filth of the daughters of Zion (Isaiah 4:4). He'evarti me-alekha avonekha, I have put away your iniquity from you, as Nathan said to David, The LORD also has put away your sin (2 Samuel 12:13). Machalatsot, festal robes, as in Isaiah 3:22. Tsanif, turban, as in my justice was like a robe and a turban (Job 29:14); tahor, clean, is the pure gold of the high priest's plate (Exodus 28:36). Then I said: the prophet speaks into his own vision; the Greek has no I said, and makes it part of the command.

  • vv6–7 "solemnly charged… keep My watch… a place to walk among these who stand here" — va-ya'ad, solemnly charged, as in The man solemnly warned us (Genesis 43:3). Mishmarti tishmor, keep My watch, the priests' duty, keep the LORD's watch, so that you do not die (Leviticus 8:35). Mahlekhim, a place to walk, is found only here: a right of way among these who stand here, the attendants of the heavenly court (v4).

  • v8 "men who are a portent: I am about to bring My servant the Branch" — anshei mofet, men who are a portent, as Isaiah said of himself and his children, signs and portents in Israel (Isaiah 8:18): the priests are themselves a sign of what is coming. Tsemach, Branch, is the name of the promised king of David's line in Jeremiah, I will raise up for David a righteous Branch (Jeremiah 23:5; 33:15). Avdi, My servant, as Zerubbabel is called in Haggai 2:23. The Greek has Anatolē, Dawn or Rising, for Branch: the Greek word means both a sprouting and the sun's rising.

  • v9 "on one stone are seven eyes… I am about to engrave its inscription… in one day" — einayim, eyes, may also be facets or springs; 4:10 explains these seven are the eyes of the LORD. Mefatteach pittuchah, word for word engraving its engraving, the verb of the high priest's plate, engrave on it, with the engravings of a seal: Holy to the LORD (Exodus 28:36). U-mashti, I will remove, from mush, depart. The Greek has I am digging a pit.

  • v10 "each of you will invite his neighbor under his vine and under his fig tree" — the words of Solomon's peace, each man under his vine and under his fig tree (1 Kings 4:25), and of Micah's promise (Micah 4:4).

chapters.title: Not by Might, Nor by Power
chapters.html:
Zechariah 4

The Lampstand and the Two Olive Trees

1The messenger who talked with me came back and roused me, like a man who is roused from his sleep.

2He said to me, "What do you see?" I said, "I see a lampstand all of gold, with a bowl on top of it and its seven lamps on it, and seven and seven pipes for the lamps that are on top of it;

3and there are two olive trees by it, one on the right of the bowl and one on its left."

4I answered and said to the messenger who talked with me, "What are these, my lord?"

5The messenger who talked with me answered and said to me, "Do you not know what these are?" I said, "No, my lord."

Not by Might

6Then he answered and said to me, "This is the word of the LORD to Zerubbabel: Not by might, nor by power, but by My Spirit, says the LORD of hosts.

7What are you, great mountain? Before Zerubbabel you will become a plain. He will bring out the top stone with shouts of 'Grace, grace to it!'"

8Then the word of the LORD came to me, saying,

9"The hands of Zerubbabel have laid the foundation of this house, and his hands will finish it. Then you will know that the LORD of hosts has sent me to you.

10For who has despised the day of small things? They will rejoice and see the tin stone in the hand of Zerubbabel. These seven are the eyes of the LORD, which run to and fro through the whole earth."

The Two Sons of Oil

11I answered and said to him, "What are these two olive trees on the right of the lampstand and on its left?"

12A second time I answered and said to him, "What are these two branches of the olive trees, beside the two golden pipes that pour out the golden oil from them?"

13He said to me, "Do you not know what these are?" I said, "No, my lord."

14He said, "These are the two sons of oil who stand by the Lord of all the earth."

Notes

  • vv1–3 "roused me, like a man who is roused from his sleep… a lampstand all of gold… two olive trees" — va-ye'ireni, roused me, the verb of 2:13, He has roused Himself. The lampstand is the tabernacle's, You shall make a lampstand of pure gold… its seven lamps (Exodus 25:31, 37), here with a gullah, bowl, as in the golden bowl (Ecclesiastes 12:6), on top. Shiv'ah ve-shiv'ah mutsaqot, seven and seven pipes, is uncertain: seven pipes for each lamp, or seven in all on each side. Written va-yomer, he said; read va-omar, I said, as the verse continues I see.

  • vv4–5 "What are these, my lord?… Do you not know what these are?" — the question and answer come twice (vv4–5, 12–13), and the answer to the trees waits until v14.

  • v6 "Not by might, nor by power, but by My Spirit" — chayil, might, is the word for an army (Joel 2:11, His army) and for wealth, and koach, power, for strength of body. Be-ruchi, by My Spirit, the Spirit of the LORD, as in My Spirit stands among you (Haggai 2:5). The word comes into the vision of the lampstand without a break, and the vision resumes at v11.

  • vv7–9 "What are you, great mountain?… a plain… the top stone… The hands of Zerubbabel have laid the foundation" — le-mishor, a plain, as in Isaiah's road home, the rough places a plain (Isaiah 40:4). Ha-even ha-roshah, the top stone, the last or first stone of the building; the Greek has the stone of inheritance. Teshu'ot chen chen lah, shouts of "Grace, grace to it!", as the people shouted with a great shout when the foundation was laid (Ezra 3:11). The promise was kept: This house was finished on the third day of the month of Adar, in the sixth year of the reign of Darius the king (Ezra 6:15).

  • v10 "who has despised the day of small things?… the tin stone… the eyes of the LORD, which run to and fro through the whole earth" — the small day is the one the old men wept over (Haggai 2:3). Ha-even ha-bedil, the tin stone: bedil is tin, as in the tin and the lead (Numbers 31:22), perhaps a weight on a builder's line; the Greek has the tin stone. Shiv'ah elleh einei YHWH, these seven are the eyes of the LORD, explains the seven eyes on the stone (3:9), and meshotetim be-khol ha-arets, run to and fro through the whole earth, are the seer's words to Asa, the eyes of the LORD run to and fro through the whole earth (2 Chronicles 16:9).

  • vv11–12 "these two branches of the olive trees… the two golden pipes that pour out the golden oil" — shibbalei, branches, is the word of an ear of grain, Shibboleth (Judges 12:6), here the clusters or spikes of the olive. Tsanterot, pipes, is found only here. Ha-zahav, word for word the gold: the oil is called gold for its color.

  • v14 "the two sons of oil who stand by the Lord of all the earth" — benei ha-yitshar, word for word sons of the fresh oil, the yitshar of the grain, the new wine and the oil (Haggai 1:11). Son of names what a thing is full of: the two are those set apart with oil, and the chapter has just named the governor (vv6–10) and the high priest (3:1–10). Adon kol ha-arets, the Lord of all the earth, as in the ark of the covenant of the Lord of all the earth (Joshua 3:11) and Micah 4:13.

The messenger who talked with me answered and said to me, "Do you not know what these are?" I said, "No, my lord."
Not by Might
Then he answered and said to me, "This is the word of the LORD to Zerubbabel: Not by might, nor by power, but by My Spirit, says the LORD of hosts.
What are you, great mountain? Before Zerubbabel you will become a plain. He will bring out the top stone with shouts of 'Grace, grace to it!'"
Then the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
"The hands of Zerubbabel have laid the foundation of this house, and his hands will finish it. Then you will know that the LORD of hosts has sent me to you.
For who has despised the day of small things? They will rejoice and see the tin stone in the hand of Zerubbabel. These seven are the eyes of the LORD, which run to and fro through the whole earth."
The Two Sons of Oil
I answered and said to him, "What are these two olive trees on the right of the lampstand and on its left?"
A second time I answered and said to him, "What are these two branches of the olive trees, beside the two golden pipes that pour out the golden oil from them?"
He said to me, "Do you not know what these are?" I said, "No, my lord."
He said, "These are the two sons of oil who stand by the Lord of all the earth."

chapters.title: The Flying Scroll
chapters.html:
Zechariah 5

The Flying Scroll

1Again I lifted up my eyes and looked, and saw a flying scroll.

2He said to me, "What do you see?" I said, "I see a flying scroll; its length is twenty cubits and its width ten cubits."

3He said to me, "This is the curse that goes out over the face of the whole land; for according to it every thief will be purged from here, and according to it everyone who swears will be purged from here.

4I have sent it out, declares the LORD of hosts, and it will enter the house of the thief and the house of the one who swears falsely by My name. It will lodge inside his house and consume it, its timbers and its stones."

The Woman in the Ephah

5Then the messenger who talked with me went out and said to me, "Lift up your eyes, please, and see what this is that is going out."

6I said, "What is it?" He said, "This is the ephah that is going out." He also said, "This is their appearance throughout the land."

7A round cover of lead was lifted, and there was a woman sitting inside the ephah.

8He said, "This is Wickedness." He threw her down inside the ephah and threw the lead weight on its mouth.

9Then I lifted up my eyes and looked, and saw two women coming out, with the wind in their wings. They had wings like the wings of a stork, and they lifted up the ephah between the earth and the heavens.

10I said to the messenger who talked with me, "Where are they taking the ephah?"

11He said to me, "To build a house for her in the land of Shinar. When it is ready, she will be set down there on her stand."

Notes

  • vv1–2 "a flying scroll; its length is twenty cubits and its width ten cubits" — megillah, scroll, open in the air, since its size can be seen. Twenty cubits by ten are the measurements of the porch before Solomon's temple, twenty cubits long, the width of the house, and ten cubits deep (1 Kings 6:3).

  • vv3–4 "This is the curse… every thief… everyone who swears… swears falsely by My name" — ha-alah, the curse, is the word for an oath and the curse that goes with it. The two sins are two of the commandments, You shall not steal (Exodus 20:15) and You shall not swear falsely by My name (Leviticus 19:12). Mi-zeh, from here, twice, may also be on one side… on the other, as the tablets were written on both their sides, on one side and on the other (Exodus 32:15): the scroll with one sin on each side. Niqqah, will be purged, is the verb that also means go unpunished. The curse will consume the house its timbers and its stones, as the law tears down a house with blight, its stones and its timbers (Leviticus 14:45).

  • vv5–6 "This is the ephah… This is their appearance throughout the land" — the ephah is a measure of grain, and here a basket of that size; the dishonest ephah is what the merchants made small (Amos 8:5). Einam, their appearance, word for word their eye, as the manna's appearance is its eye (Numbers 11:7). The words answer the eyes of the LORD, which run to and fro through the whole earth (4:10): what the LORD's eyes see in the land is this. The Greek has This is their iniquity, avonam, a single letter different.

  • vv7–8 "A round cover of lead… This is Wickedness… threw the lead weight on its mouth" — kikkar, a round cover, is also the word for a talent, a weight; the Greek has a talent of lead. Ha-rish'ah, Wickedness, is a woman, since the word is feminine; the Greek has lawlessness. Even ha-oferet, word for word the stone of lead, the weight that seals her in.

  • vv9–11 "wings like the wings of a stork… a house for her in the land of Shinar… on her stand" — ruach, the wind, in their wings, lowercase. The chasidah, stork, is listed among the unclean birds (Leviticus 11:19). Shinar is the land of Babel's tower, where the builders found a valley in the land of Shinar (Genesis 11:2). Bayit, house, is also a temple, and mekhunatah, her stand, is close to the word for the bronze stands of Solomon's temple (1 Kings 7:27): Wickedness is carried out of the land to be housed and set up in Babylon.

chapters.title: The Man Whose Name Is the Branch
chapters.html:
Zechariah 6

Four Chariots

1Again I lifted up my eyes and looked, and saw four chariots coming out from between the two mountains; the mountains were mountains of bronze.

2With the first chariot were red horses, with the second chariot black horses,

3with the third chariot white horses, and with the fourth chariot dappled horses, strong ones.

4I answered and said to the messenger who talked with me, "What are these, my lord?"

5The messenger answered and said to me, "These are the four winds of the heavens, going out after presenting themselves before the Lord of all the earth.

6The one with the black horses is going out to the land of the north; the white ones went out after them, and the dappled ones went out to the land of the south.

7The strong ones went out and sought to go and walk about over the earth." He said, "Go, walk about over the earth." So they walked about over the earth.

8Then he called out to me and spoke to me, saying, "See, those that go out to the land of the north have set My Spirit at rest in the land of the north."

A Crown for Joshua

9The word of the LORD came to me, saying,

10"Take from the exiles, from Heldai, from Tobijah and from Jedaiah, who have come from Babylon, and go that same day to the house of Josiah son of Zephaniah.

11Take silver and gold, make crowns, and set them on the head of Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest.

12Say to him: This is what the LORD of hosts says: Here is a man whose name is the Branch; he will branch out from his place, and he will build the temple of the LORD.

13It is he who will build the temple of the LORD; he will bear majesty, and will sit and rule on his throne. There will be a priest on his throne, and a counsel of peace will be between the two of them.

14The crowns will be for Helem, Tobijah and Jedaiah, and for Hen son of Zephaniah, as a memorial in the temple of the LORD.

15Those who are far away will come and build in the temple of the LORD; and you will know that the LORD of hosts has sent me to you. This will come to pass if you listen to the voice of the LORD your God."

Notes

  • vv1–3 "four chariots… mountains of bronze… red… black… white… dappled horses, strong ones" — the last vision answers the first: horses of colors again (1:8), now with chariots. Berudim, dappled, is the word of Jacob's flocks, striped, speckled, and dappled (Genesis 31:10). Amutsim, strong, may be a further color; in v7 it stands alone, the strong ones. The Greek has dappled grey for it.

  • vv4–5 "These are the four winds of the heavens… the Lord of all the earth" — ruchot, winds, as in 2:6, like the four winds of the heavens, and in Daniel's vision, the four winds of heaven were stirring up the great sea (Daniel 7:2); the same word means spirits. Me-hityatsev al, after presenting themselves before, is the verb of the heavenly court in Job, the sons of God came to present themselves before the LORD (Job 1:6). The Lord of all the earth, as in 4:14.

  • vv6–7 "to the land of the north… after them… to the land of the south… walk about over the earth" — the red horses of v2 are not sent anywhere. El achareihem, after them, follows the Hebrew; it might also be read to the west, behind the one who faces east, but the text does not say so. Le-hithallekh ba-arets, walk about over the earth, the patrol of 1:10–11.

  • v8 "have set My Spirit at rest in the land of the north" — heniḥu et ruchi, set My Spirit at rest. Ruach is also temper, as in their anger against him subsided (Judges 8:3), and heniach is the verb Ezekiel uses with wrath, I will satisfy My wrath on you (Ezekiel 16:42). The Greek has have given rest to My anger. The land of the north is Babylon (2:6–7).

  • vv10–11 "Heldai… Tobijah… Jedaiah… make crowns, and set them on the head of Joshua" — Yeda'yah, Jedaiah, is also the name of a priestly house among the returned exiles, the sons of Jedaiah, of the house of Jeshua (Ezra 2:36). Atarot, crowns, is plural; in v14 the same word takes a singular verb, and Job uses the plural for one crown, I would bind it on me as a crown (Job 31:36). The Greek has crowns here and the crown in v14.

  • vv12–13 "a man whose name is the Branch; he will branch out from his place… There will be a priest on his throne" — the Branch promised in 3:8, tsemach with its verb, yitsmach, he will branch out. Hod, majesty, is the authority Moses put on Joshua son of Nun (Numbers 27:20). The verse is crowning Joshua the priest, but the Branch builds the temple, as Zerubbabel does (4:9). Ve-hayah kohen al kis'o may be he will be a priest on his throne, one man, or there will be a priest on his throne, a second, as the two of them suggests; the Greek has the priest will be at his right hand.

  • vv14–15 "Helem… Hen son of Zephaniah, as a memorial… if you listen to the voice of the LORD your God" — Helem is Heldai of v10, and Hen is Josiah son of Zephaniah; chen means favor, and the Greek reads for the favor of the son of Zephaniah. Ve-hayah im shamoa tishme'un be-qol YHWH eloheikhem are the words of Deuteronomy 28:1, if you listen, listen to the voice of the LORD your God, where the blessings follow; here the sentence stops after the if.

chapters.title: Was It for Me That You Fasted?
chapters.html:
Zechariah 7

A Question About Fasting

1And it came to pass in the fourth year of King Darius that the word of the LORD came to Zechariah on the fourth day of the ninth month, Kislev.

2Bethel had sent Sharezer and Regem-melech and his men to plead with the LORD,

3saying to the priests of the house of the LORD of hosts and to the prophets, "Should I weep in the fifth month and keep myself apart, as I have done these many years?"

4Then the word of the LORD of hosts came to me, saying,

5"Say to all the people of the land and to the priests: When you fasted and mourned in the fifth month and in the seventh these seventy years, was it for Me that you fasted?

6When you eat and when you drink, is it not you who eat and you who drink?

7Are not these the words that the LORD called out through the former prophets, when Jerusalem was inhabited and at ease, with its cities around it, and the Negev and the lowland were inhabited?"

Judge with True Justice

8The word of the LORD came to Zechariah, saying,

9"This is what the LORD of hosts says: Judge with true justice, and show loyal love and compassion each to his brother.

10Do not oppress the widow or the fatherless, the guest or the poor; and let none of you plan evil in your heart against his brother."

11But they refused to pay attention; they turned a stubborn shoulder and made their ears heavy so as not to hear.

12They made their hearts diamond, so as not to hear the instruction and the words that the LORD of hosts had sent by His Spirit through the former prophets. So great wrath came from the LORD of hosts.

13"As He called and they would not listen, so they will call and I will not listen," says the LORD of hosts,

14"and I scattered them with a whirlwind among all the nations they had not known. The land was left desolate behind them, with no one coming or going; they made the pleasant land a desolation."

Notes

  • v1 "in the fourth year of King Darius… the ninth month, Kislev" — two years after the visions (1:7). Kislev is named also in Nehemiah 1:1.

  • vv2–3 "Bethel had sent Sharezer and Regem-melech… to plead with the LORD… Should I weep in the fifth month" — Beit El Sar-etser ve-Regem melekh may be read as here, the town of Bethel sending two men, or as one name, Bethel-sharezer, who sent Regem-melech; the Greek has Sarasar and Arbeseer the king, sent to Bethel. Le-challot et penei YHWH, to plead with the LORD, as Moses pleaded with the LORD his God (Exodus 32:11). The fifth month is when the temple was burned (2 Kings 25:8). Hinnazer, keep myself apart, is the verb of the Nazirite, who vows to keep himself apart for the LORD (Numbers 6:2). The town speaks as one person: I.

  • vv5–6 "in the fifth month and in the seventh… was it for Me that you fasted?" — the seventh month is when Gedaliah was killed at Mizpah (2 Kings 25:25). Ha-tsom tsamtuni ani, word for word did you fast Me, Me?: the LORD's I is stressed. Isaiah asks the same, Is such the fast that I choose (Isaiah 58:5). The question about fasting is answered in 8:19.

  • vv9–10 "Judge with true justice… loyal love and compassion… the widow or the fatherless, the guest or the poor" — chesed, loyal love, with rachamim, compassion, as in Micah 6:8, to love loyal love. The list of the helpless is Jeremiah's, if you do not oppress the guest, the fatherless and the widow (Jeremiah 7:6), with the poor added.

  • vv11–12 "they turned a stubborn shoulder… made their hearts diamond… by His Spirit through the former prophets" — va-yittenu khatef soraret, they turned a stubborn shoulder, as Nehemiah's prayer says, They turned a stubborn shoulder (Nehemiah 9:29), the ox that will not take the yoke. Shamir, diamond, as in with a point of diamond it is engraved on the tablet of their heart (Jeremiah 17:1). Be-rucho, by His Spirit: the Spirit spoke through the prophets. Ha-torah, the instruction.

  • vv13–14 "As He called and they would not listen, so they will call and I will not listen… I scattered them with a whirlwind" — the LORD speaks of Himself as He and then as I in one sentence; the Hebrew has both. Wisdom says the same, Then they will call on me, but I will not answer (Proverbs 1:28). Ve-esa'arem, I scattered them with a whirlwind, from sa'ar, a storm. Erets chemdah, the pleasant land, as in they despised the pleasant land (Psalm 106:24).

chapters.title: Ten Men Will Take Hold
chapters.html:
Zechariah 8

I Have Returned to Zion

1The word of the LORD of hosts came, saying,

2"This is what the LORD of hosts says: I am exceedingly jealous for Zion, and I am jealous for her with great wrath.

3This is what the LORD says: I have returned to Zion and will dwell in the middle of Jerusalem. Jerusalem will be called the City of Truth, and the mountain of the LORD of hosts the Holy Mountain.

4This is what the LORD of hosts says: Old men and old women will again sit in the streets of Jerusalem, each with his staff in his hand because of his great age.

5The streets of the city will be full of boys and girls playing in its streets.

6This is what the LORD of hosts says: If it is too wondrous in the eyes of the remnant of this people in those days, should it also be too wondrous in My eyes? declares the LORD of hosts.

7This is what the LORD of hosts says: I am about to save My people from the land of the east and from the land of the setting sun.

8I will bring them, and they will dwell in the middle of Jerusalem; they will be My people, and I will be their God, in truth and in righteousness.

Let Your Hands Be Strong

9This is what the LORD of hosts says: Let your hands be strong, you who in these days hear these words from the mouth of the prophets who spoke on the day the foundation of the house of the LORD of hosts was laid, that the temple might be built.

10For before those days there was no wage for man and no wage for beast, and no peace from the enemy for anyone going out or coming in; I set every man against his neighbor.

11But now I will not be to the remnant of this people as in the former days, declares the LORD of hosts.

12For there will be a sowing of peace: the vine will give its fruit, the land will give its produce, and the heavens will give their dew; and I will give the remnant of this people all these things as their inheritance.

13And it shall come to pass that, as you were a curse among the nations, house of Judah and house of Israel, so I will save you, and you will be a blessing. Do not be afraid; let your hands be strong.

14For this is what the LORD of hosts says: As I purposed to do you harm when your fathers provoked Me to wrath, says the LORD of hosts, and I did not relent,

15so again in these days I have purposed to do good to Jerusalem and to the house of Judah. Do not be afraid.

16These are the things you shall do: Speak the truth each to his neighbor; in your gates judge with truth and with justice that makes peace.

17Let none of you plan evil in your heart against his neighbor, and do not love a false oath; for all these are things that I hate, declares the LORD."

Fasts Will Become Feasts

18The word of the LORD of hosts came to me, saying,

19"This is what the LORD of hosts says: The fast of the fourth month, the fast of the fifth, the fast of the seventh and the fast of the tenth will become joy and gladness for the house of Judah, and cheerful feasts. So love truth and peace.

20This is what the LORD of hosts says: Peoples will yet come, and those who live in many cities.

21Those who live in one city will go to another, saying, 'Let us go at once to plead with the LORD and to seek the LORD of hosts. I am going too.'

22Many peoples and strong nations will come to seek the LORD of hosts in Jerusalem and to plead with the LORD.

23This is what the LORD of hosts says: In those days ten men from all the languages of the nations will take hold, they will take hold of the edge of the garment of a Jewish man, saying, 'Let us go with you, for we have heard that God is with you.'"

Notes

  • vv2–3 "I am exceedingly jealous for Zion… I have returned to Zion… the City of Truth" — the words of 1:14 and 1:16, I am exceedingly jealous for Jerusalem and for Zion… I have returned to Jerusalem with compassion, now with chemah gedolah, great wrath: the heat of His jealousy is for her. Ir ha-emet, the City of Truth; emet is also faithfulness, and Isaiah promised Jerusalem would be called the Faithful City (Isaiah 1:26). Emet comes back in vv8, 16 and 19.

  • vv4–6 "Old men and old women… boys and girls playing… should it also be too wondrous in My eyes?" — the two ends of life together in the streets, where the city once had neither. Yippale, too wondrous, is the word the LORD spoke to Abraham, Is any word too wondrous for the LORD? (Genesis 18:14), and to Jeremiah, Is anything too wondrous for Me? (Jeremiah 32:27).

  • vv7–8 "from the land of the east and from the land of the setting sun… they will be My people, and I will be their God" — from sunrise to sunset, the whole earth. The covenant words, as in the new covenant of Jeremiah, I will be their God, and they will be My people (Jeremiah 31:33), here be-emet u-vi-tsedaqah, in truth and in righteousness.

  • vv9–12 "Let your hands be strong… the prophets who spoke on the day the foundation… was laid… the heavens will give their dew" — the prophets of that day are Haggai and Zechariah (Ezra 5:1), and be strong is Haggai's word (Haggai 2:4). Zera ha-shalom, a sowing of peace, word for word the seed of peace, is obscure; the Greek has I will show peace. The promise undoes the curse in Haggai, the heavens have held back the dew, and the earth has held back its produce (Haggai 1:10), in the words of the law's blessing, the land will give its produce, and the trees of the field will give their fruit (Leviticus 26:4).

  • v13 "as you were a curse among the nations… so I will save you, and you will be a blessing" — the word to Abraham, Be a blessing (Genesis 12:2), given back after exile. Judah and Israel are named together.

  • vv14–15 "As I purposed to do you harm… and I did not relent, so again… I have purposed to do good" — zamam, purposed, as in 1:6, As the LORD of hosts purposed to do to us. Nicham, relent, as when God relented of the evil He had said He would do (Jonah 3:10); here He did not relent then, and now He has again purposed, shavti, word for word I have turned, the verb of 1:3, Return to Me… and I will return to you.

  • vv16–17 "Speak the truth each to his neighbor… do not love a false oath" — the curse of the flying scroll was on the one who swears falsely by My name (5:4). Plan evil in your heart, the words of 7:10.

  • v19 "The fast of the fourth month, the fast of the fifth, the fast of the seventh and the fast of the tenth" — the answer to Bethel's question (7:3). The four fasts mourn the fall of Jerusalem: in the tenth month the siege began (2 Kings 25:1), in the fourth the city was breached (Jeremiah 39:2), in the fifth the temple burned (2 Kings 25:8), and in the seventh Gedaliah was killed (2 Kings 25:25).

  • vv20–23 "Let us go at once to plead with the LORD… ten men… will take hold of the edge of the garment of a Jewish man" — nelkhah halokh, word for word let us go, going: at once. The pleading of Bethel (7:2) is now the nations'. Many peoples and strong nations, as in Micah's strong nations far away (Micah 4:3). Kenaf, the edge, is the corner of a garment, where the law put the tassels, make tassels on the corners of their garments (Numbers 15:38). Ish yehudi, a Jewish man, as Mordecai is first named (Esther 2:5). Elohim immakhem, God is with you, the promise of Haggai 1:13, I am with you.

But now I will not be to the remnant of this people as in the former days, declares the LORD of hosts.

For there will be a sowing of peace: the vine will give its fruit, the land will give its produce, and the heavens will give their dew; and I will give the remnant of this people all these things as their inheritance.
And it shall come to pass that, as you were a curse among the nations, house of Judah and house of Israel, so I will save you, and you will be a blessing. Do not be afraid; let your hands be strong.
For this is what the LORD of hosts says: As I purposed to do you harm when your fathers provoked Me to wrath, says the LORD of hosts, and I did not relent,
so again in these days I have purposed to do good to Jerusalem and to the house of Judah. Do not be afraid.
These are the things you shall do: Speak the truth each to his neighbor; in your gates judge with truth and with justice that makes peace.
Let none of you plan evil in your heart against his neighbor, and do not love a false oath; for all these are things that I hate, declares the LORD."
Fasts Will Become Feasts
The word of the LORD of hosts came to me, saying,

"This is what the LORD of hosts says: The fast of the fourth month, the fast of the fifth, the fast of the seventh and the fast of the tenth will become joy and gladness for the house of Judah, and cheerful feasts. So love truth and peace.
This is what the LORD of hosts says: Peoples will yet come, and those who live in many cities.
Those who live in one city will go to another, saying, 'Let us go at once to plead with the LORD and to seek the LORD of hosts. I am going too.'
Many peoples and strong nations will come to seek the LORD of hosts in Jerusalem and to plead with the LORD.

This is what the LORD of hosts says: In those days ten men from all the languages of the nations will take hold, they will take hold of the edge of the garment of a Jewish man, saying, 'Let us go with you, for we have heard that God is with you.'"
